trials.note: No verified peer-reviewed publication was located for this trial. The evidence located is conference or registry material only, so the record carries no primary_ref, no pubs, no result, no enrolment figure and no digest. Status is awaited because no reported result was verified, not because the source document states a trial state. The axes are taken from the source document's design line, a randomised phase 2 comparison, and its story line; the document gives no primary endpoint, so endpoint is omitted. The 1L tag rests on the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT04603183, which requires no prior systemic therapy for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease. Progression on or within 36 months of completing adjuvant endocrine therapy is one of its aggressive-disease criteria, and the record still calls the study regimen first-line. Carried from the source document as an interpretive limit, an early response to induction chemotherapy is not a universal answer for every visceral-crisis scenario, and the eligibility and the treatment sequence must be preserved whenever the trial is cited.

trials.endpoint: Change in Ki67 between baseline and Day 15, the day of surgery.
trials.result: Relative change from baseline in Ki67 was a geometric least-squares mean of -75.9% (95% CI -81.9 to -67.9) for amcenestrant 400 mg, -68.2% (-75.7 to -58.4) for amcenestrant 200 mg and -77.7% (-83.4 to -70.0) for letrozole. trials.note: The publication does not state a trial phase. This is a 14-day preoperative window study with a pharmacodynamic endpoint, so it measures proliferation suppression and not disease outcome, and it cannot stand in for an adjuvant efficacy trial. n is the safety population of 104 who received at least one dose; the Ki67 comparison rests on the modified intent-to-treat population of 95 with paired values. Enrollment was stopped early for slow recruitment during the COVID-19 pandemic, so the arms are smaller than planned.

trials.topic: a brain-penetrating peptide-drug conjugate for recurrent brain metastases and leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
trials.population: Adults with measurable recurrent brain metastases from breast cancer, with or without leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, most of them heavily pretreated.
trials.arms: Single arm of ANG1005 600 mg/m2 intravenously every 3 weeks, with no control arm.
trials.endpoint: Intracranial objective response rate, assessed by CNS RECIST 1.1.
trials.result: The intracranial objective response rate was 15 percent by investigator assessment and 8 percent by independent radiology facility review. The study preset rule for intracranial objective response rate by independent review was not met, and there was no comparator arm.
trials.os: In the leptomeningeal carcinomatosis subset the estimated median overall survival was 8.0 months (95% CI 5.4 to 9.4). No overall survival figure is reported for the whole cohort, and the comparison the authors draw is with historical control rather than a randomised arm.
trials.note: Single-arm study with no randomised comparator for either the parenchymal or the leptomeningeal population. The primary endpoint was formally negative, in that the preset rule for intracranial objective response rate by independent radiology facility review was not met, and the investigator-assessed rate of 15% and the independent rate of 8% should be read separately rather than merged. The 28-patient leptomeningeal carcinomatosis group is a subset of the 72 enrolled patients, so its disease control and survival figures are subgroup results, and the authors' claim of prolonged survival there rests on a comparison with historical control. The abstract gives no NCT identifier and states no hormone receptor or HER2 restriction, so the subtype axis is all comers. The line is tagged any because entry turned on recurrent brain metastases, and the mean of 2.8 prior CNS-directed therapies is not a count of prior systemic lines.

trials.topic: dual checkpoint blockade in a rare histology, metaplastic breast carcinoma
trials.population: Patients with unresectable or metastatic metaplastic breast cancer, median age 60 years and a median of 2 prior lines of therapy, range none to five.
trials.arms: Single arm of ipilimumab 1 mg/kg intravenously every 6 weeks plus nivolumab 240 mg intravenously every 2 weeks.
trials.endpoint: Objective response rate.
trials.result: The objective response rate was 18%, 3 of 17 patients, with 1 complete and 2 partial responses, which met the primary endpoint; the three responses were ongoing at 28+, 33+ and 34+ months. Median progression-free survival was 2 months.
trials.os: Median overall survival was 12 months.
trials.note: This is one cohort of a rare-tumour basket study rather than a stand-alone trial, and the key is suffixed with the population so that other DART cohorts can be registered separately. Eligibility turned on metaplastic histology rather than receptor status, and the publication describes the majority of tumours as triple-negative without restricting entry to them, so the subtype axis is all rather than TNBC even though the record is cross-referenced from metastatic triple-negative disease. Entry required progression after at least one line of standard therapy, so the patients counted at zero prior lines met it with curative-setting chemotherapy, which counts as a line, and the line tag is 2L,3L+. The result is carried by a subset, three exceptional and still ongoing responses against no activity in the rest, in 17 patients, and all three responders developed adrenal insufficiency. A single-arm cohort of this size is a signal in a rare histology and should not be read across to unselected triple-negative disease.

trials.topic: denosumab versus zoledronic acid for established bone metastases
trials.population: Advanced breast cancer with at least one bone metastasis. 1026 patients were assigned denosumab and 1020 zoledronic acid.
trials.arms: Subcutaneous denosumab 120 mg with intravenous placebo versus intravenous zoledronic acid 4 mg adjusted for creatinine clearance with subcutaneous placebo, each every 4 weeks.
trials.endpoint: Time to first on-study skeletal-related event, tested for non-inferiority and then for superiority.
trials.result: Denosumab delayed time to first skeletal-related event, hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.71 to 0.95), P = .01 for superiority. For first and subsequent events the rate ratio was 0.77 (95% CI 0.66 to 0.89), P = .001.

trials.prior_therapy: Ongoing stable disease or response after at least three cycles of first- or second-line platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease; the maintenance continues that line.
trials.topic: chemotherapy-free maintenance after platinum-sensitive disease, with or without PD-L1 blockade
trials.population: Patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer, defined as estrogen and progesterone receptor expression of 10% or less, with ongoing stable disease or a complete or partial response to first- or second-line platinum-based chemotherapy.
trials.arms: Olaparib 300 mg twice daily alone versus olaparib plus durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1 every 4 weeks, randomized 1:1, each arm judged against a historical control rather than against the other.
trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival compared with a historical control of continued platinum-based therapy.
trials.result: Median progression-free survival from randomization was 4.0 months (95% CI 2.6 to 6.1) with olaparib and 6.1 months (95% CI 3.7 to 10.1) with olaparib plus durvalumab, both significantly longer than the historical control (P = 0.0023 and P < 0.0001 respectively). Clinical benefit rates were 44% (95% CI 23% to 66%) with olaparib alone and 36% (95% CI 17% to 59%) with the combination.
trials.os: Secondary endpoint. Median overall survival was 21.7 months with olaparib alone and 18.3 months with olaparib plus durvalumab, after deaths in 11 of 23 and 8 of 22 patients. The trial was not designed to compare the arms with each other.
trials.note: Randomized but non-comparative. Each arm was tested against a historical control of continued platinum-based chemotherapy and the trial was not powered for a head-to-head comparison, so the longer median in the combination arm is not evidence that durvalumab adds benefit. Triple-negative disease was defined at estrogen and progesterone receptor expression of 10% or less and 3 of the 45 patients had expression of 1% to 10%, so the subtype tag is broader than a strict zero-expression definition. Maintenance followed first- or second-line platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease, and randomisation was stratified by that line, so the line tag is 1L,2L. Of the 45 patients, 37 were treated in the first-line setting. Germline BRCA mutation was not required and the authors single out a BRCA wild-type subset with durable disease control. Overall survival was a secondary endpoint, with medians of 21.7 months with olaparib and 18.3 months with the combination, and median follow-up was 9.8 months.

trials.arms: Single arm of trastuzumab deruxtecan at the recommended doses for expansion, 5.4 or 6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks, in the breast cancer cohorts of a first-in-human dose-escalation and dose-expansion study.
trials.endpoint: Safety and preliminary activity, the proportion of patients with a confirmed objective response; the HER2-low figure is by independent central review and the HER2-positive figure by investigator.
trials.result: HER2-low cohort: confirmed objective response by independent central review in 20 of 54 patients, 37.0% (95% CI 24.3% to 51.3%), median duration of response 10.4 months. HER2-positive cohort after trastuzumab emtansine: confirmed objective response in 66 of 111 evaluable patients, 59.5% (95% CI 49.7% to 68.7%). Single arm, no control.
trials.os: HER2-low cohort: median 29.4 months (95% CI 12.9 to 29.4), from the PMC full text. The HER2-positive cohort abstract gives no overall survival. Single arm, so there is no comparison.
trials.note: Single-arm first-in-human study with no comparator, so the response rates are activity signals rather than evidence of benefit over standard treatment. n is the 169 patients with breast cancer treated at the recommended doses for expansion, 54 with HER2-low and 115 with HER2-positive disease; the HER2-positive response is among the 111 evaluable for activity. The two breast cohorts were published separately, the HER2-low cohort in 2020 (the primary_ref) and the HER2-positive cohort in 2019. The registry's DESTINY-Breast01 is the separate phase 2 registration study, not this trial. Three HER2-low patients, all at 6.4 mg/kg, died of drug-induced interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, and 5.4 mg/kg was taken forward. 87% of the HER2-low cohort had hormone receptor-positive disease (PMC full text). trials.endpoint: Rate of a preoperative endocrine prognostic index score of 0, PEPI-0, at surgery.
trials.note: No clinical results publication was located for this trial, which the investigators registered as NCT02712723. A correlative single-cell genomics paper from the trial group (Griffiths 2021, Nat Cancer) confirms the design but does not report the PEPI-0 endpoint. The record therefore carries no primary_ref, no pubs and no result, and no figures are recorded. What the source document states is that early proliferation suppression with ribociclib did not translate into an improved PEPI-0 rate; that is a conference report, and it must be cited as such rather than as a peer-reviewed trial report. Do not cite unrelated ribociclib laboratory papers as the trial report. The phase comes only from the source document's design line, which reads randomised phase II and nothing further. The correlative paper confirms the neoadjuvant setting, the ER-positive, HER2-negative subtype and the comparison of letrozole with placebo or ribociclib. Its sample size rests on the rate of PEPI-0 scores, which supports the recorded endpoint. The topic is inferred from the story line, and n, year, population and arms are omitted until a clinical results publication states them.

trials.topic: olaparib in place of carboplatin alongside paclitaxel in HRD-selected HER2-negative disease
trials.population: Patients with untreated primary HER2-negative breast cancer, cT2-cT4a-d or cT1c with node-positive or sentinel-node-positive disease or cT1c triple-negative or cT1c with Ki-67 above 20%, all with homologous recombination deficiency defined by a high HRD score and/or a germline or tumour BRCA1/2 mutation.
trials.arms: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 weekly plus olaparib 100 mg twice daily for 12 weeks vs paclitaxel plus carboplatin AUC 2 weekly for 12 weeks, both followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide.
trials.endpoint: Pathological complete response, ypT0/is ypN0, tested by a two-sided one-group chi-square test planned to exclude a pCR rate of 55% or lower in the paclitaxel plus olaparib arm.
trials.result: pCR 55.1%, 90% CI 44.5 to 65.3, with paclitaxel plus olaparib against 48.6%, 90% CI 34.3 to 63.2, with paclitaxel plus carboplatin. The trial could not exclude a pCR rate of 55% or lower in the olaparib arm, so the primary endpoint was not met.
trials.os: 4-year overall survival 89.2% with paclitaxel plus olaparib against 96.9% with paclitaxel plus carboplatin, hazard ratio 3.27, 95% CI 0.39 to 27.20, log-rank P = 0.244, at median follow-up 49.8 months.
trials.note: The tabulated result is the pathological complete response from the 2020 primary report; the 2025 publication reports the long-term survival endpoints, which were secondary, and supplies the os field. The design was a one-group test against a fixed threshold, not a formal comparison or an equivalence trial, so the arm-to-arm differences are descriptive only. Eligibility was HER2-negative disease selected by homologous recombination deficiency, so hormone receptor-positive patients were enrolled alongside triple-negative ones. The survival signal runs against olaparib and is concentrated in patients without a BRCA1/2 mutation, on very small event counts and with confidence intervals that cross one throughout.

trials.population: Patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior anticancer therapies for metastatic disease, and in a separate cohort women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer progressing after endocrine-based therapy and at least one chemotherapy for metastatic disease.

trials.result: Triple-negative cohort, 108 patients: objective response 33.3% (95% CI 24.6 to 43.1; 3 complete, 33 partial), median duration of response 7.7 months, clinical benefit rate 45.4%, median progression-free survival 5.5 months. trials.os: Triple-negative cohort: median 13.0 months (95% CI 11.2 to 13.7). Hormone receptor-positive cohort: median 12 months (95% CI 9.0 to 18.2). Single arm, so there is no comparison.
trials.note: Single-arm basket trial with no comparator, so the response rates are activity signals. n is 162: the 108 patients with triple-negative disease who received 10 mg/kg after at least two prior therapies (the primary_ref), and the 54 women in the prespecified hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative cohort reported separately in 2020. The 2017 report of the first 69 triple-negative patients is an earlier analysis of the same cohort. The 2019 response figures are by local assessment; post hoc blinded central review gave 34.3% and a median duration of response of 9.1 months. The randomised confirmations are ASCENT and TROPiCS-02, separate registry records.

trials.note: Single arm, so the figures establish that activity exists and not how often it will be seen. Two androgen receptor thresholds are in play and they are not the same thing. Entry required staining above 0%, while the evaluable subgroup required at least 10% of nuclei, which is the threshold TBCRC 011 and TBCRC 032 used for entry. The published overall response rate of 64% is printed with a 95% CI of 77% to 98%, an interval that cannot bracket its own point estimate, so only the point estimate is carried into the row. trials.result: pCR 45.8%, 95% CI 32.0 to 60.6, in the evaluable population and 49.2%, 95% CI 36.7 to 61.6, in the intention-to-treat population. Eligibility required a germline BRCA1/2 mutation as well as triple-negative disease, so both tags apply.

trials.topic: dual checkpoint blockade selected by tumour mutational burden
trials.population: Patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and a high tumour mutational burden, at least 9 mutations per megabase.
trials.arms: Single arm of nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus low-dose ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks, given for 2 years or until progression.
trials.endpoint: Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1.
trials.result: Among 30 patients enrolled, the median tumour mutational burden was 10.9 mutations per megabase (range 9 to 110) and the confirmed objective response rate was 20%. In the prespecified correlative analysis the 6 patients with a burden of at least 14 mutations per megabase had a higher response rate, 60% versus 12% below that threshold (p = 0.041).
trials.os: Overall survival was a secondary endpoint and no overall survival figures are reported in the abstract.
trials.note: Selection was by tumour mutational burden alone within HER2-negative disease, so hormone receptor-positive patients were enrolled alongside triple-negative ones and the record is tagged across both; the abstract does not give the split. The full text allowed none to three prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease, so the line tag is 1L,2L,3L+. Hormone receptor-positive patients needed endocrine progression in the metastatic setting or recurrence on adjuvant endocrine therapy, and that endocrine phase counts as one line. The threshold subgroup that carries the selection message is 6 patients and is a prespecified correlative outcome rather than a randomised comparison, so it does not establish a universal tumour mutational burden cut-off. The trial was funded by Bristol Myers Squibb.

trials.population: Heavily pretreated women with HER2-mutated metastatic breast cancer that was HER2-negative on local testing, enrolled as one cohort of an open-label basket study of HER2-altered solid tumours; those with hormone receptor-positive disease also received fulvestrant.
trials.arms: Single arm of tucatinib plus trastuzumab, with fulvestrant added for hormone receptor-positive disease.
trials.endpoint: Overall response rate.
trials.result: Overall response rate was 41.9% (90% CI 26.9 to 58.2) in the 31 patients. The secondary endpoints of duration of response and progression-free survival were 12.6 months (90% CI 4.7 to not estimable) and 9.5 months (90% CI 5.4 to 13.8) respectively.
trials.os: Secondary endpoint. Median overall survival was 20.1 months (90% CI 15.9 to not estimable) in this single-arm cohort, with 11 deaths, and the authors describe the data as immature.
trials.note: This is the HER2-mutated breast cohort of a solid-tumour basket study rather than a stand-alone breast trial, and it is single-arm. Entry required an activating HER2 mutation in disease that was HER2-negative by conventional local testing, so it is not a HER2-amplified or first-line HER2-positive trial and belongs with molecular-target evidence. The subtype tag is HR+/HER2-,TNBC because the cohort took both hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative patients within HER2-negative disease. Only the hormone receptor-positive patients received fulvestrant, and the full text gives response separately, 12 of 27 hormone receptor-positive and 1 of 4 receptor-negative patients. The abstract reports the duration of response and progression-free survival figures without naming a statistic, so the record does not call them medians. Confidence intervals are 90%, not the registry's usual 95%, and the cohort of 31 is small. Patients were heavily pretreated, but entry required only one previous line for locally advanced or metastatic disease and the full text gives a median of 3 (range 1 to 7) such lines, so the line tag is 2L,3L+.

trials.note: A basket study of 13 patients with breast cancer and 7 with other solid tumours; n records the breast cancer cohort only, because that is the figure the abstract gives for breast cancer and no combined analysed total is stated. Entry required wild-type BRCA1 and BRCA2 with a mutation in another homologous recombination gene, so despite sitting in the PARP grouping this is not a germline BRCA trial and it carries no BRCA subtype tag. Eligibility was any HER2-negative disease and the abstract does not give the hormone receptor split, so the record is tagged across hormone receptor-positive and triple-negative disease. The full text required progression on at least one line of therapy for advanced disease with no upper limit, and patients had received a median of two prior lines (range 1 to 8), so the line tag is 2L,3L+. The abstract does not designate a primary endpoint, so overall response rate is taken as primary from the order in which the efficacy results are presented. The response figures rest on four responders among 13 patients and the gene-specific signal is confined to germline PALB2, so the result does not validate homologous recombination genes or deficiency scores as interchangeable biomarkers.

trials.population: Women with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and active brain metastases, 35 entered with untreated brain metastases and 12 with brain metastases progressing after local radiotherapy.
trials.arms: Single arm of bevacizumab 15 mg/kg on day 1 with utidelone 30 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5, every 3 weeks, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
trials.endpoint: Central nervous system objective response rate by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1.

trials.note: This is the first prospective cohort of any size in HER2-negative breast cancer with active brain metastases. It reports its response rate under two sets of criteria in the same patients, which is the only place in this cell where the criteria can be compared without also changing the cohort. The untreated and post-radiotherapy strata are described at entry but no response rate is given for each separately. Entry was defined by the state of the brain disease, and the abstract sets no limit on prior systemic lines, so the line is tagged any.

trials.topic: twelve weeks of anthracycline-free nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy, carboplatin versus gemcitabine, with response used to guide further treatment
trials.population: Patients with triple-negative breast cancer, oestrogen and progesterone receptor under 1% and HER2-negative, cT1c to cT4c, cN0 or node-positive.
trials.arms: Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 with gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks versus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 with carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks, each for 12 weeks.
trials.endpoint: Pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0) by therapy arm; the trial was also powered for early response, defined as a Ki-67 decrease of more than 30% or fewer than 500 invasive tumour cells in the three-week serial biopsy.
trials.result: Pathological complete response was 28.7% (95% CI 0.22 to 0.36) with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine and 45.9% (95% CI 0.38 to 0.54) with nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin, 95% CI for the difference 6.2% to 27.9%, P = .002. Pathological complete response was lower in early non-responders than in early responders, 19.5% versus 44.4%, P < .001, and was 50.0% in patients whose early response was unclassifiable.
trials.os: no survival advantage from carboplatin at a median follow-up of 60 months despite the higher pathological complete response rate, HR 1.04 (0.68-1.59); the final analysis does not report overall survival separately from invasive disease-free survival
trials.note: The tabulated result is the primary pathological complete response comparison from gluz2018. The final analysis, gluz2022, reports no survival advantage for carboplatin despite its higher pathological complete response rate, hazard ratio 1.04 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.59), so the pathological complete response gain here did not become a survival gain. Treatment after the 12 weeks was response-adapted, with omission of further chemotherapy allowed only after pathological complete response, so between-arm survival comparisons are confounded by what patients received next. gluz2022 is indexed in PubMed as an editorial but is the trial's final survival and translational report, and no overall survival figures are given in either abstract. Neither trial report prints an NCT identifier; NCT01815242 is from the ADAPT umbrella protocol, hofmann2013adapt, and is confirmed by ClinicalTrials.gov.

trials.topic: rapidly cycled tandem high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell support against dose-dense conventional chemotherapy
trials.population: high-risk breast cancer with nine or more positive axillary lymph nodes
trials.arms: two cycles of dose-dense epirubicin-cyclophosphamide then two cycles of high-dose epirubicin, cyclophosphamide and thiotepa with peripheral-blood stem-cell support vs four cycles of dose-dense EC then three cycles of dose-dense CMF
trials.endpoint: event-free survival
trials.result: 4-year event-free survival 60% (53-67) with tandem high-dose vs 44% (37-52) with dose-dense conventional chemotherapy, P = 0.00069, by intention to treat
trials.os: 4-year overall survival 75% (69-82) with tandem high-dose vs 70% (64-77) with dose-dense conventional chemotherapy, P = 0.02
trials.note: The result runs against other trials of high-dose chemotherapy, which the authors attribute partly to the tandem design with a brief induction. The cited biomarker paper is a retrospective analysis of 236 tumours suggesting the benefit concentrated in triple-negative and grade 3 disease.

trials.topic: recurrence score and chemotherapy omission
trials.population: HER2-negative early breast cancer, pT1 to pT4c, node-positive or node-negative with at least one high-risk feature.
trials.arms: Four cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by four cycles of docetaxel versus six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide.
trials.endpoint: Disease-free survival, tested for noninferiority with a margin of 4.4%.
trials.result: Five-year disease-free survival was 89.6% with epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel versus 89.9% with six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide. The difference was within the prespecified noninferiority margin of 4.4%.
trials.os: Five-year overall survival was 94.5% with epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel versus 94.7% with six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide.
trials.note: 3198 patients were enrolled, 2449 were randomised to the chemotherapy comparison, and the recurrence score 11 or lower chemotherapy omission cohort that the filing refers to was a nonrandomised 348-patient group.

trials.topic: palbociclib plus exemestane and OFS versus capecitabine
trials.population: Premenopausal women aged 19 years or older with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer progressing on tamoxifen, performance status 0 to 2.
trials.arms: Palbociclib plus exemestane with leuprolide ovarian suppression versus capecitabine.
trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival.
trials.result: Median progression-free survival was 20.1 months with palbociclib plus exemestane and ovarian suppression versus 14.4 months with capecitabine, hazard ratio 0.659, one-sided p=0.0235.
trials.os: In the 2025 analysis, median overall survival was 54.8 months with palbociclib plus endocrine therapy versus 57.8 months with capecitabine, hazard ratio 1.02, p=0.92. There was no overall survival difference.
trials.note: About half of patients in each group were treatment naive for metastatic disease, but all had relapsed or progressed on tamoxifen, which counts as a line even when given as adjuvant therapy. With one chemotherapy line for metastatic disease also allowed, the line axis is 2L,3L+.

trials.prior_therapy: HER2-positive advanced disease scheduled for T-DM1 with no stated line rule; exceptional responders in the final report had none to six prior treatments.
trials.topic: HER2-PET to predict T-DM1 benefit
trials.population: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, immunohistochemistry 3+ or fluorescence in situ hybridisation ratio at least 2.2, scheduled to start trastuzumab emtansine.
trials.arms: Single arm. Pretreatment HER2 positron emission tomography with zirconium-89 labelled trastuzumab, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography at baseline and before cycle 2, in patients all receiving trastuzumab emtansine.
trials.endpoint: Negative and positive predictive values of HER2 positron emission tomography, of early metabolic response, and of the two combined, against morphological response by RECIST 1.1 after three cycles and against time to treatment failure.
trials.result: HER2 imaging was negative in 29% of patients and showed intrapatient heterogeneity in 46%. Negative and positive predictive values against RECIST were 88% and 72% for HER2 imaging and 83% and 96% for early metabolic response. Combining the two gave predictive values of 100% in both directions and separated a group with median time to treatment failure of 2.8 months from one with 15 months. There was no control arm and no randomised allocation by imaging.
trials.os: Not reported. The primary publication reports predictive values and time to treatment failure only.
trials.note: Entry required HER2-positive advanced disease scheduled for trastuzumab emtansine, and neither report states a rule on prior lines, so the line is any. The final report describes exceptional responders who had received from none to six prior treatments.
